- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce peak forecasts by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecasted peaks at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and price is trending up, model under-forecasts; add 3–5% to forecasted mean to account for sentiment drag.
- Model consistently over-forecasts in early 30-day windows when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply a 2–4% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.5 to -0.5 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; force mean reversion to 1–2 days before true price turns.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extrapolating from 18-day history; use 30-day moving average as baseline, then adjust for sentiment momentum.
